snippets.output: Chlamydia trachomatis has evolved mechanisms to evade the host immune system and can persist within host epithelial cells, making spontaneous resolution unlikely.
snippets.pattern_notes: Immune evasion + persistence cause unlikely spontaneous resolution—causal chain.

snippets.output: Most women with genital tract chlamydial infections are asymptomatic, making it more challenging to diagnose and treat promptly.
snippets.pattern_notes: Asymptomatic nature causes diagnostic/treatment challenge—cause/effect link.

snippets.output: Untreated chlamydia can lead to severe reproductive complications, including pelvic inflammatory disease, tubal factor infertility, and ectopic pregnancy.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerates the complications (PID, infertility, ectopic pregnancy) of untreated chlamydia.

snippets.output: Chlamydia trachomatis infections often do not resolve on their own and can cause permanent reproductive damage if left untreated, although some bacterial infections may occasionally resolve without treatment.
snippets.pattern_notes: Lists properties of chlamydia infections: non-resolution, damage potential, with contrast to other bacterial infections.
